So I have a similar experience as the girl who did the paper. Back in 2018 I started attending the university to get a degree in history, and during my first few months of my degree I had to write a paper on if it's a good idea to either save or change history by removing monuments etc. I did follow the instructions to my understanding, but I also interjected my own opinion which was extremely inflammatory and without sources. I was graded very low, barely passed, and the teacher had written a longer note to meet her after class to discuss it. She politely explained to me it was because I may have misunderstood since every opinion, even my own, must be sourced in some way to back up my claims as Academia is supposed to be neutral and based on more factual evidence (ie. recorded findings, primary sources, secondary sources) and the only reason why she didn't outright fail me for my dismissal and name-calling of other people's opinions was because she wants me to do better next time. 

So, while I did take her advice a bit too roughly at the time, I graduated in 2022 (after a years delay due to corona) with a paper heavily focused on framing my own opinion on a matter with almost no prior research and using secondary and primary sources from "close enough" topics to argue my own point. I also had changed my views significantly during this time, because turns out reading more papers and actually having to argue with myself for hours why I'm right or wrong challenges the perspective of oneself. 

It's nothing to do with "free speech", it's to do with how academia works. The teacher was right to fail their paper, the same way mine could have. (Granted, I'm in Europe sooo..)

comments.text:
I taught community college and undergrad, I've also published and presented medical research internationally and have needed to defend my research to those both in and outside my own culture.

I read her paper. I wouldve called her in and said, hey do you think this adheres to the assignment and is your best work? You sure you wanna submit this? And then give her an extension to rewrite it with some notes. If she refused id give it a 1 because I always give assignments a minimum of a 1 if they atleast handed something in.

Why? Because 1) everyonevhas beliefs that are different, but if you decide to put them out there as reasoning for something then you MUST be able to defend them and explain why it's pertinent. 2) If you're ever to treat patients or clients and go against standard protocol and prosecutes you MUST be able to defend yourself successfully because you could end up having to defend yourself in court. 3) most assignments in college isn't about the actual content, but about learning how to process, apply, and communicate critical thinking skills. If you're gonna make a claim you need to know how to defend it and how to research it. In philosophy and most sciences there is a saying that you know write your thesis statement until you've finished your paper, because the point is the apply logic and known concepts to a question or issue and determine something. Often you won't know the answer until afterwards, and if you think you know the answer then you're ego is taking over your reasoning. 

Finally, as a trans person myself, I could care less if my students agreed or not with my existence; but if they wanna make it an issue I usually ask them to explain why and defend their perspective to me directly so they have to experience vocalizing their opinion about a human being to a human being.
